title: Sentryline Q4 ops, cost & SLA alignment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled

Summary:
Quick operational QBR-style checkin to reconcile Sentryline's Q4 traffic forecast, cost targets, and SLA requirements. Main asks: confirm dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs at their projected scale, validate latency baselines with their sample payload, and confirm compliance docs for procurement. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- Current footprint and forecast (p95, concurrency, batch patterns)
- Cost targets and gating metrics for Dedicated pilot
- SLA/uptime and fallback policies (region failover, model variants)
- Security/compliance checklist for procurement (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- Technical baseline: latency/throughput test plan and schedule

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, im the account lead for Sentryline. Omar from infra is with me. Jordan, Priya, Damon, good to see you.
[00:09] Jordan Reyes: Hi Maya, thanks. Yep got Priya and Damon here, quick on time but we have a packed agenda.
[00:15] Omar Patel: Hey all. We'll try to run through the ops items first then move into the pilot pricing.
[00:22] Priya Menon: Sounds good. For context, we've got a large retail customer pilot in November — expecting bursts up to 600 concurrent sessions, p95 token latency target around 300ms, and overall cost target about 40% lower than current cloud endpoints.
[00:36] Damon Liu: And finance flagged a hard cap on monthly inference spend for Q4 — we need an estimate to the dollar before next Fri for our procurement window.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Got it. We'll cover rough math today and Omar will propose the test plan to lock down real numbers. Quick question — are you currently using batching on your side or sending mostly single-turn requests?
[00:55] Jordan Reyes: It's a mix, 70% single-turn chat style requests, 30% multi-turn. There is some client-side batching but it's minimal. We're open to SDK changes for better batching but prefer server-side improvements.
[01:10] Omar Patel: That's helpful. For single-turn heavy workloads, dedicated capacity often yields predictable p95 at scale because we can reserve GPUs and tune batching thresholds; hosted can be cheaper on low baseline but variance is higher.
[01:25] Priya Menon: Can you quantify variance? We care about percent of requests breaching 500ms more than 0.1% of the time.
[01:32] Omar Patel: Ballpark: hosted with autoscaling and mixed-tenant pools, you might see tail events during noisy neighbor spikes — we've seen p99 jumps to ~800ms in worst-case multi-tenant peaks at very high concurrency. Dedicated with reserved nodes plus burst buffers keeps p99 under 450ms in our internal profiles. But we'll run Sentryline's sample to validate.
[01:50] Damon Liu: Ok, that's a useful frame. For procurement we also need compliance: SOC2 type II, SSO SAML, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs retention of 13 months. Can Redwood provide those?
[02:05] Maya Chen: Yes — SOC2 and ISO paperwork we can share; SAML SSO and RBAC are supported on the enterprise plan; KMS integration and audit logs with configurable retention are in the Private/Dedicated offering. I'll send the security pack after the call.
[02:18] Jordan Reyes: Great, please include the VPC/private control-plane notes — we might need a VPC private deployment because of data residency rules for that retail pilot.
[02:26] Omar Patel: Noted. For VPC/private, we'll need a short checklist from your infra team — firewall rules, peering, allowed IPs — we'll attach a template.
[02:36] Priya Menon: On the cost math: can we see a worked example with your recommended model for our workload (single-turn heavy) — E2E token rates, batch sizing, and expected spend at 600 concurrency?
[02:47] Maya Chen: Yes, Omar, do you want to run through a quick sample calc now?
[02:50] Omar Patel: Sure. If we assume average request is 120 tokens output, 30 tokens input, so 150 tokens total; at 600 concurrent with mean request rate of 0.5 rps per session gives roughly 450 tokens/sec sustained. With dedicated A100-style pool and continuous batching, our internal unit economics estimate is about X tokens/sec per GPU — (note: internal kernel variance) — translating to ~8-10 GPUs for predictable p95; that maps to $Yk/month — I'll follow up with exact numbers after we run their payload through our baseline runner.
[03:20] Jordan Reyes: Can you avoid sharing the internal X and Y numbers in the notes? We prefer concrete final numbers.
[03:24] Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll convert to a friendly summary and send concrete pricing.
[03:28] Damon Liu: Also, are there penalties or credits if SLAs aren't met on Dedicated? Procurement asked about refund policy.
[03:36] Maya Chen: We have SLA terms on Dedicated contracts; credits for sustained breaches are standard in the enterprise plan, we can include specific thresholds in the pilot paperwork.
[03:44] Priya Menon: Technical deep dive: Omar, can you explain how fallback policies work if a region has capacity issues? We need predictable behavior: either degrade to a smaller model variant or route to another region.
[03:55] Omar Patel: We support policy-based routing: you can define sequence: try local dedicated variant, if capacity insufficient, fallback to compatible quantized variant, then fallback region. Each step is configurable and tracked in the console with tracing. Note that routing across regions increases latency, and you can opt for a circuit-breaker to fail early.
[04:13] Jordan Reyes: Ok good. Would prefer a model-variant fallback rather than cross-region for this retail pilot to avoid surge latency.
[04:20] Omar Patel: Makes sense. We'll show the option in the runbook.
[04:24] Damon Liu: Procurement also asked for exportable audit logs showing token counts per-invocation for billing reconciliation. Do you provide that?
[04:33] Maya Chen: Yes, per-request granularity logs are available for enterprise customers and can be exported; we can also produce a summarized billing CSV on a cadence you choose.
[04:40] Priya Menon: Great. Next on the agenda: test plan. Omar?
[04:45] Omar Patel: Test plan: 1) Sentryline shares one week of anonymized traffic and a sample payload generator; 2) Redwood runs a baseline with current hosted profile and with a dedicated pool (mirrors of their expected concurrency) — capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput and token cost; 3) Run a stress test with burst pattern to validate autoscale and tail behavior; 4) Deliver a benchmark spreadsheet and recommendation. Timeline: if we get traffic by Friday (2026-10-24), we can return results by 2026-10-28.
[05:10] Jordan Reyes: That timeline works — we'll try to get data by EOD Friday. Small note: traffic includes some streaming responses — can you support token-streaming metrics?
[05:20] Omar Patel: Yes, streaming is supported; we'll include stream-specific latency accounting (first-byte latency, last-byte).
[05:25] Priya Menon: Are there any quota or VIP onboarding steps for dedicated pools? How long to provision?
[05:30] Maya Chen: Typical provisioning for Reserved Dedicated is 2-5 business days once contract and capacity are agreed; for quick pilots we can provision a smaller dedicated pool within 24-48 hours in many regions.
[05:41] Damon Liu: Ok that helps with procurement scheduling.
[05:45] Jordan Reyes: Quick question — we also evaluate competitors: Anthropic was mentioned internally as a potential vendor, and we have some talks with a cloud partner. Any notes on how Redwood compares on reliability and cost?
[05:56] Maya Chen: Short answer: we focus on predictable inference economics with tooling for batching and caching; competitors often trade simplicity for less deterministic tail behavior. We'll include a short competitive snapshot in the follow-up.
[06:06] Priya Menon: Please do.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Quick recap before next steps. Omar will run the baseline once you send sample workload. I'll send SOC2 and the security packet, and a dedicated pilot pricing sheet. Damon — we'll include SLA terms and credit language for your procurement team.
[06:23] Damon Liu: Thanks. Also please cc our procurement alias procurement@sentryline.com when you send docs.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Noted.
[06:31] Jordan Reyes: Anything else?
[06:33] Omar Patel: One small technical note: we recommend enabling KV cache for multi-turn sessions to reduce tokens and latency — small ops change but often cuts per-conversation tokens by 15-30%.
[06:45] Priya Menon: That's interesting — would require client SDK update. Add that to the tech notes.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Will do.
[06:52] Jordan Reyes: Great. Let's confirm next meeting — how about a 30-minute check-in the week after results, Tuesday 2026-11-02 10:00 PT?
[07:00] Maya Chen: Works for us.
[07:03] Damon Liu: Works.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deliverables.

(Transcript contains some auto-caption errors in proper nouns and token counts; speakers sometimes overlap.)
